video_title: OpenAI’s New Agent Stack: Computer Use, Decisions API, UltraFast, Dots—Ari Weinstein & Nikunj Handa
gist: Dev Day conversation with OpenAI's Ari Weinstein and Nikunj Handa on computer-use agents (now faster than average humans, cheaper on GPT-6.1), the new Decisions API cloned from Jev on Luna weights in about four weeks, and API platform work on caching, compaction and the agents API.

insights.claim: OpenAI's computer use agents are now faster than the average human at most tasks, and Ari Weinstein says the next frontier is superhuman speed, matching or beating expert computer users, which would enable real-time products.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Speed parity unlocks real-time agent UX and defaulting to delegation instead of manual work.
insights.quote: computer use is like faster at accomplishing tasks than like the average human probably in [music] in most cases

insights.claim: The biggest computer-use improvement over the past year is recovery: models used to start tasks reliably but stall on problems, and now debug, retry and introspect on what is failing.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Error recovery, not initiation, was the reliability bottleneck for long-running agents.

insights.claim: Modern OpenAI computer use writes and executes JavaScript to perform many actions per step and mixes screenshots, accessibility trees and Playwright depending on the task, instead of one click per screenshot.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Harness design (code-as-action plus multimodal interfaces) drives speed gains as much as the model.

insights.claim: Direct DOM and accessibility access lets the model see an entire page or app at once, eliminating the old screenshot-scroll-screenshot loop; Weinstein calls this the biggest single 'aha' alongside many small speed 'paper cuts'.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Representation efficiency (token-efficient accessibility dumps) is a moat-like engineering detail.

insights.claim: As computer use gets faster, it is increasingly bottlenecked by external latency such as waiting for sites like DoorDash to load, and by non-event-driven waits like customer-service bot replies taking 30 seconds to 3 minutes.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Further speedups depend on event-driven triggering and the speed of the third-party software itself, not only the model.

insights.claim: OpenAI trains its models on its own computer-use harness, so developers using the in-distribution harness via the new agents API may get speed, cost and accuracy advantages over custom harnesses.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Raises the cost of building custom agent harnesses on OpenAI models and favors first-party scaffolding.

insights.claim: Computer use lets the coding agent test the software it built, closing the develop-test loop so the human no longer acts as QA; a visual play-test skill is cited as catching design issues code review misses.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Agent self-QA is a key productivity unlock for coding agents.

insights.claim: Computer use makes cloning SaaS apps screen by screen feasible: the agent captures every screen and Codex rebuilds it, which the host frames as a way to kill a poor SaaS product.
insights.so_what: Pressure on weak incumbent SaaS whose moat is only UI and workflow, as agents drive and replicate them.

insights.claim: Creators and users are using computer use to automate platforms with no API (YouTube A/B testing and community posts), and Weinstein cut a two-hour meal-prep order to 15 minutes, eight times faster than manual.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Closed platforms without APIs become automatable by agents, weakening API-access as a gate.

insights.claim: The new GPT-6.1 model is described as one fifth the cost of Astra overall and one seventh the cost for computer use specifically, with a keynote claim of 7x faster computer use.
insights.speaker: Ari Weinstein
insights.so_what: Large per-task cost drops for agentic workloads widen viable use cases and pressure competitors' pricing.

insights.claim: OpenAI's inference team cut the Luna price by about 80% through inference improvements over a couple of months, then shifted focus to maximum speed, yielding the Ultrafast tier on Astra now available in the API.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: Inference efficiency is compounding and price/speed tiers are becoming product differentiators.

insights.claim: WebSockets, first launched for GPT-5.3 Codex Spark, underpin async tool calling, mid-turn steering and async reasoning in GPT-6 by removing round-trip overhead between model and tools.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: Bidirectional transport is becoming core agent infrastructure.

insights.claim: Hosts note GPT-5.3 Spark was explicitly attributed to Cerebras while the guests neither confirmed nor denied whether Ultrafast uses Cerebras hardware; the host also notes OpenAI has its own silicon.
insights.so_what: Hardware supplier for OpenAI's fastest tier remains unconfirmed; relevant to the Cerebras read-through.

themes.theme: Decisions API as a Jev-style fast classifier

insights.claim: The Decisions API is built on the same Luna weights with no new model trained: reasoning off, structured output constraints, and an optimized inference stack that runs multiple questions in parallel as a batch; it is priced like Luna.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: A fast-classifier product was shipped in about four weeks with existing weights, showing how cheaply frontier labs can clone startup features.

insights.claim: OpenAI built the Decisions API within roughly four weeks of being inspired by Jev, with an inference engineer and an infra engineer prototyping it; the host called OpenAI the first frontier lab to clone and adopt it.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: Frontier labs rapidly absorb popular niche API ideas, a competitive risk for startups like Jev.

insights.claim: Nikunj Handa argues the Jev differentiation lies beyond the API shape: speed, accuracy and confidence calibration, which OpenAI has not yet addressed and may need a future model release to hill-climb.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: Calibration quality, not API clones, is where a defensible edge for fast decision models would sit.

insights.claim: Decisions API use cases cited include support-ticket classification, pairing with GPT Live (talker/thinker split) to make voice tool calls faster, and low-latency LLM-as-judge evals; it is weaker than Astra on long-horizon computer use.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: Fast small models become the routing and reaction layer in multi-model agent systems.

themes.theme: API platform: caching, compaction, higher-level primitives

insights.claim: OpenAI offers guaranteed cache hits within 30 minutes, has a 12-hour caching guarantee in preview, and added cache pre-warming, aimed at long-running single-thread personal agents.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: Cache-aware design is a major cost lever for persistent agents; pay-for-guarantee caching creates a new pricing dimension.

insights.claim: For context management OpenAI offers server-side compaction at a token threshold in the Responses API and manual /compact, and the agents API builds proprietary compaction into the harness; file-based compaction techniques are being tested in Codex.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: Context ceilings near a million tokens persist, so compaction remains a core agent layer.

insights.claim: Nikunj Handa, formerly at Stripe, frames OpenAI's API strategy as building higher-level primitives (agents API, memory vaults, storage) on low-level primitives, and the host likens it to building AI-native EC2 and S3 for an AI cloud.
insights.speaker: Nikunj Handa
insights.so_what: OpenAI is moving up the stack into agent infrastructure, competing with middleware and harness vendors.
